# Install Node.js with nvm on Ubuntu 20.04

> Install a production-ready Node.js environment on Ubuntu 20.04 using nvm for flexible version management. You will install nvm, select a Node.js LTS version, and verify your setup is ready for development.

**Generated by [BuildBridge](https://github.com/researchsite)**

## Prerequisites

- **Ubuntu 20.04**: `N/A — OS requirement`
- **curl**: `sudo apt install curl`

## Steps

### 1. Install nvm (Node Version Manager)
```bash
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
```
> Installs nvm into ~/.nvm and adds shell hooks

### 2. Reload shell configuration
```bash
source ~/.bashrc
```
> Or open a new terminal window

### 3. Verify nvm is installed
```bash
nvm --version
```

### 4. Install the latest LTS version of Node.js
```bash
nvm install --lts
```
> Use 'nvm install 20' to pin a specific version

### 5. Set the default Node.js version
```bash
nvm alias default node
```
> Makes this version the default for new shell sessions

### 6. Verify Node.js and npm are installed
```bash
node --version && npm --version
```

### 7. Run a quick test script
```bash
node -e "console.log('Node.js is ready!')"
```
